claims.text: A new ab initio method will incorporate vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed method will substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The method is intended to treat high-entropy systems in both solid and fluid states.
Incorporating vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling will improve computational efficiency.
The proposed method will maintain accuracy while improving computational efficiency.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by 50% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy compositions in a high-temperature regime.
The achieved cost reduction may depend on the implementation and the particular system studied.
The method should be benchmarked against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD on a set of high-entropy systems.
Failure to reduce computational cost by at least 30% falsifies the hypothesis.
Failure to maintain thermodynamic-property accuracy within 5% of the baseline methods falsifies the hypothesis.
